checkpoints.note: After the HEADERS block is parsed successfully and the request is not header-terminated, the stream enters `RECV_BODY`. That admits subsequent DATA frames on this stream into the vulnerable request-body path.

First project parser step that decodes the attacker-controlled HEADERS frame, materializing the HPACK block and frame flags that open the HTTP/2 request stream later driven into the vulnerable body-handling path.

The DATA-frame rejection logic checks only whether the stream left `RECV_BODY`; it does not also reject the case where the request-body callback slot has already been cleared after END_STREAM. The fix extends this condition to `stream->state != H2O_HTTP2_STREAM_STATE_RECV_BODY || !stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb`.
